steps.claim: §7.1 defines memory as "Byte-addressed, little-endian, sparse" and permits alloc n whenever the bump range and allocation-table checks pass. §10 hostcall requires its byte interval to lie in one live allocation; §7.3 console.write(ptr,len) has the same memory-range precondition. With ptr_width=H=64, heap_base=1, heap_limit_max=2^63 and A_tab=1, allocating n=2^63 is legal: the end is 2^63+1 <= 2^64 and one entry fits. The resulting transfer length is legal; concrete host storage may fail but must not become a panic or false memory fault.

Two independently pinned canonical objects use n = const.i64 9223372036854775808; p = alloc n. The CC object then executes r = hostcall org.bennett.test p n; ret r, with the service declared. The R object executes effect console.write p n; ret, with console version 0.8 declared. Both check successfully.
